advances: An all-normal raw credit for arbitrary actual anchored relations and simultaneous allocation at one fixed mark.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write $U_j$ for the captured volume in fiber $z_j$, and $S=\sum_jU_j$. If $S\ge\min_j V_j$ the credit bound is immediate because $R(h)\le\min_j V_j$. Otherwise all the strict complementary cuts in these fibers have positive volume. Their weighted Minkowski combination lies in the strict complement at $p$, by convexity of $C$ and affinity of the defining halfspace inequality. Apply Brunn–Minkowski first to their nonempty compact inner subcuts with affine margin at most $-\varepsilon$, and let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ by continuity from below. This applies also to purely base normals, for which the positive strict complements are whole fibers. It gives
$$
h^{1/d}\ge\sum_j\lambda_j(V_j-U_j)^{1/d}.
$$
If $S=0$ this gives $\Delta(h)=0$. Otherwise, for $0\le s\le S$, the functions $f_j(s)=\lambda_j[v_j-(V_j-s)^{1/d}]$ are nonnegative convex and vanish at zero. Thus
$$
\Delta(h)\le\sum_j f_j(U_j)\le\sum_j(U_j/S)f_j(S)\le\max_j f_j(S).
$$
For $\Delta(h)>0$ a maximizing $j$ has $f_j(S)\ge\Delta(h)$ and $S<V_j$, so $\Delta(h)<\lambda_jv_j$ and inversion gives $S\ge V_j-(v_j-\Delta(h)/\lambda_j)^d\ge R(h)$. The zero-deficit case gives the same bound trivially. The range, continuity and monotonicity follow from the formula.

For scalar exactness, if $R(h)=0$, all-zero captures satisfy the root inequality because $\Delta(h)=0$. If $0<R(h)<\min_jV_j$, spend $R(h)$ entirely on a minimizing index. No root there vanishes, and the root inequality holds with equality by inversion. If $R(h)=\min_jV_j$, fully capture an index of minimum volume. This invokes the full-fiber escape alternative. These allocations solve the relaxation based on the two alternatives, whose feasible capture vectors can be larger than those generated by actual halfspaces.

At a fixed mark of ordinary depth at least $\delta$, the own capture of any containing halfspace is at least $\delta$, also for a pure-base normal. Its anchor residual is at most $V_p-\delta$, so each relation supplies its credit at that bound by monotonicity. Multiply the relations by feasible $\theta_e$ and add. Each other fiber capture is counted at most once, so this combined credit plus the own capture is a lower bound on the total cap mass. The feasible coefficient set is closed, nonempty, and bounded since every relation has a nonempty source set, hence every $\theta_e\le1$. The maximum exists and is uniform over containing caps. The full-mass centroid theorem 6769574fc1bd9f8d supplies $\delta=\Gamma_d V_p$, and substitution under root equality gives the stated deficit. If the actual maximum is below the given threshold, every proved lower budget at an actual centroid is below it as well.
statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge1$, with actual positive-volume integer fibers at $p,z_1,\ldots,z_m$, the $z_j$ distinct and different from $p$. Suppose $p=\sum_j\lambda_jz_j$ with $\lambda_j>0$ summing to one. Put $V_j=|K_{z_j}|$, $v_j=V_j^{1/d}$, $\Delta(h)=(\sum_j\lambda_jv_j-h^{1/d})_+$, and
$$
R(h)=\min_j\big[V_j-(v_j-\Delta(h)/\lambda_j)_+^d\big].
$$
For every closed ambient halfspace $H$, if $h$ is the volume outside $H$ in the anchor fiber, the sum of the captured volumes in the $z_j$ is at least $R(h)$. The credit is continuous, nonincreasing, and lies in $[0,\min_jV_j]$. It is exact as a scalar lower bound under the alternatives of full-fiber escape or the positive-residual root inequality.

For a mark $y\in K_p$ of ordinary raw depth at least $\delta>0$, let $\mathcal E$ be a finite collection of anchored relations at $p$ with credits $R_e$ and source sets $J_e$ as above. The raw mixed depth of $(p,y)$ is at least
$$
\delta+\max_{\theta\ge0,\ \sum_{e:z\in J_e}\theta_e\le1\ (z\ne p)}
\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\theta_e R_e(V_p-\delta).
$$
The maximum is attained. At the ordinary centroid use $\delta=\Gamma_d V_p$ with $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. If $\sum_j\lambda_jv_j=V_p^{1/d}$ for one relation, its root deficit at this argument is $V_p^{1/d}[1-(1-\Gamma_d)^{1/d}]$. If the maximum mixed raw depth is less than $\Gamma_d W/k$ for total volume $W$ and $k$ occupied parity classes, the displayed centroid budget is strictly below $\Gamma_d W/k$ at every positive anchor.
title: All-status anchored residual credits and fractional packing at one mark
